sar.narrative: Between 2016-12-22 and 2016-12-29, card C11923-K2 belonging to customer C11923 was used for 25 transaction(s) totalling $2,609.02, of which the transaction that triggered this investigation was $131.30 on 2016-12-29, and the activity was conducted online under product code C from the device profile 'SM-G610F Build/NRD90M | unknown | chrome 66.0 for android | unknown'. The cardholder contacted the bank stating they did not make this purchase, and 59 transactions occurred on this card in the 48 hours ending at the flagged one, while 3 online authorisations under $5 on this card in the 24h before the flagged transaction, followed by a larger purchase, match the testing sequence policy R5 describes. The same device profile was used by 2 other card(s) in the thirty days to 2016-12-29, specifically C03938-K1 and C05595-K1, indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder, and the bank's closed investigations already record 10 confirmed fraud case(s) on this card (CC-4501, CC-3905, CC-3206, CC-3039). We assumed that the activity is suspicious because it is consistent with testing of a stolen card number before use, assessed at a 84% probability of being fraudulent on 6 independent pieces of evidence drawn from the transaction graph and the institution's closed-case history, and we further assumed that the filing is made because the loss exposure of $2,609.02 exceeds the institution's $1,000 reporting threshold. The pending authorisation has been declined, step-up authentication has been required for further activity, the card has been blocked and scheduled for reissue, an internal investigation case has been opened, the card has been placed under heightened monitoring, and the cards sharing the same origin have been placed under monitoring, while the 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one (CC-4800, CC-0290, CC-5285, CC-3576, CC-3473) closed as 5 confirmed fraud (card not present fraud, card not present new device, card testing) and 0 cleared.
